bank.title: Python Session 6 — Production Bank 001

questions.question: Which statement best describes `Average Function` according to the taught session?

options.text: A function can aggregate a list of numbers and return their average.
The function scans words and returns the longest one encountered.
The taught `is_prime(n)` checks divisibility up to the square root and returns a Boolean.
Two functions convert Celsius↔Fahrenheit and return converted numeric values.

explanation.ar: A function can aggregate a list of numbers and return their average.

questions.question: Which taught function/pattern is most appropriate when you want to calculate the average of a list?

options.text: longest-word scan
sum(numbers) / len(numbers)
is_prime(n)
celsius_to_fahrenheit / fahrenheit_to_celsius

explanation.ar: `sum(numbers) / len(numbers)` is the course-aligned choice for this task: calculate the average of a list.

questions.question: What output is shown for the taught average example?

explanation.ar: The trace follows the taught `Average Function` behavior: A function can aggregate a list of numbers and return their average.

questions.question: A learner divides by a fixed number that does not match the list length. What correction best matches the course?

options.text: Use `longest-word scan` instead regardless of the goal.
Ignore the issue because `Average Function` has no rules.
Convert the task to `Prime Function` without changing the logic.
Divide the total by the actual number of values, as in the taught average pattern.

explanation.ar: Divide the total by the actual number of values, as in the taught average pattern.
